name: Taylor Johnson
headline: Software Engineer · AI Systems & Developer Tools
summary: Software engineer focused on making complex systems understandable and efficient through explicit representations, typed contracts, and reproducible tests. My work connects real-time grid state coordination, production HPC authentication, and AI evaluation and execution infrastructure.

bullets: Investigated and documented a production HPC platform, tracing OIDC, JWT, and LDAP identity flows through Apache modules, Nginx per-user processes, and Lua authentication hooks.
Built a Docker reproduction of the authentication stack to debug behavior without privileged production access; investigated configuration layers and security-sensitive URL handling.
Turned authentication and infrastructure findings into reproducible debugging procedures and documentation for onboarding and platform maintenance.
Built React/Recoil state coordination for real-time electric-grid incident analysis, synchronizing multiple relay data feeds for reliability-sensitive operator interfaces.
Extended Chart.js with draggable temporal annotations and implemented COMTRADE relay-data processing for electrical disturbance analysis.
Integrated dynamic windowed diagnostic layouts with react-mosaic, keeping timing, state consistency, and debugging clarity central to the interface.
Taught Python, JavaScript, React, and computer science concepts to students ages 10–16; helped students debug programs and development environments through hands-on instruction.

projects.name: Attune
bullets: Built a typed repository-analysis instrument in Flix with Grit extraction and bounded Datalog queries; separated semantic policy from narrow Java/native interfaces and pinned the Bazel/Nix build.

Designed reproducible localization and review evaluations with gold-free prediction inputs, frozen receipts, exact memoization, and shared Bazel artifacts; integrated BuildBuddy remote caching and execution.

Measured scheduling and replay costs: historical AttuneFlix offline evaluation preserved results across 61 JS/TS cases while reducing 4,301 seconds of sequential shard work to 51.7 seconds of cold remote wall time; exact replay made no new provider calls.

Built an installable agent-tool contract pipeline using DeepSeek Harness and Typert, rejecting unsupported schemas; validated transport/tool boundaries alongside semantic laws, renderer checks, and six README examples regenerated from real extraction.

projects.name: SearchBench
bullets: Built a Go/Pkl experiment surface and Python evaluation harness to compare coding-agent search strategies using typed tasks, scoring models, backend adapters, and reproducible run bundles.
Recorded search quality, token usage, cost, and classified failures so candidate strategies can be compared against a baseline with inspectable evidence.

additionalProjects.name: Local Inference Experiments
additionalProjects.text: Modified llama.cpp’s Qwen embedding path on Apple M2/Asahi Linux with Vulkan. Removed unnecessary language-model-head work, preserving bit-identical vectors in the tested comparison; throughput improved from ~72.2 to ~78.8 tokens/s (~9%).

additionalProjects.name: AI Program Optimization
additionalProjects.text: Investigated DSPy Flex/GEPA executable-program optimization and compiler-feedback validation; implemented compatibility patches for recursive tool schemas and NumPy lazy imports. Kept candidate selection separate from evaluation.

additionalProjects.name: Static Control Plane
additionalProjects.text: Modeled Crossplane/KCL infrastructure with Nix-pinned schema generation, GitOps resources, and validation before deployment.

additionalProjects.name: NixOS Infrastructure
additionalProjects.text: Built declarative multi-node NixOS deployments with provisioning, Tailscale, distributed builds, and binary caching.

additionalProjects.name: nftables Structure Fuzzer
